title: Config change canary metric gates — proposed thresholds (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
body:
Context
- Used by “Safe apply + rollback mechanism” for Optimize config changes (batching/caching/quantization/routing knobs).
- These are DEFAULT canary metric gates. Product/Eng can tighten per-tenant; loosening requires explicit override and justification.
- Gates are evaluated during canary apply, before promoting to 100% of scope.

How to read this sheet
- Gate condition compares canary vs baseline.
  - Baseline = same scope (route/model/cluster) over the 30 minutes immediately prior to canary start, excluding known incident windows.
  - Canary = traffic subset for same scope during canary window.
- If any “Blocker” gate fails → auto-abort promotion; keep canary pinned; allow one-click rollback.
- If only “Warning” gates fail → require manual acknowledgment to promote.
- Evaluation window defaults:
  - Canary duration: 10 minutes minimum AND >= 50k tokens or >= 1k requests (whichever first), capped at 30 minutes.
  - Gate sampling interval: 1 minute; require 3 consecutive failing datapoints to trip (unless otherwise specified).

TAB: Default thresholds by environment/tier
| Environment | Deployment tier | Canary traffic fraction | Promotion steps | p95 latency (ms) gate | p99 latency (ms) gate | Error rate gate (5xx + timeouts) | Saturation gate (GPU / queue) | Quality/Evals (optional) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Staging | All | 50% | 50% -> 100% | Blocker: +25% vs baseline OR +150ms (whichever higher) | Blocker: +30% OR +250ms | Blocker: +1.0% absolute OR 2x baseline (min baseline floor 0.2%) | Warning: GPU util +15pp sustained OR queue p95 +30% | N/A by default | Staging is for functional regressions; allow more perf movement. Still blocks on obvious breakage. |
| Prod | Hosted (default) | 5% | 5% -> 25% -> 100% | Blocker: +10% OR +80ms | Blocker: +12% OR +120ms | Blocker: +0.30% absolute OR 1.5x baseline (baseline floor 0.10%) | Blocker: GPU util +10pp sustained (>= 10 min) OR queue p95 +20% | Warning: eval score -1.0% relative (if enabled) | Hosted tends to have heterogeneous traffic; require token/request minimums before evaluating. |
| Prod | Hosted (high criticality routes) | 2% | 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% | Blocker: +7% OR +60ms | Blocker: +10% OR +90ms | Blocker: +0.20% absolute OR 1.3x baseline (baseline floor 0.08%) | Blocker: GPU util +8pp OR queue p95 +15% | Blocker: eval score -2.0% relative (if enabled) | Used for auth, payments-adjacent, and “core chat” routes. Tag via route metadata. |
| Prod | Dedicated (SLA tenants) | 5% | 5% -> 25% -> 100% | Blocker: +8% OR +70ms | Blocker: +10% OR +110ms | Blocker: +0.15% absolute OR 1.25x baseline (baseline floor 0.05%) | Blocker: GPU util +8pp OR queue p95 +15% | Warning: eval score -1.0% relative (if enabled) | Dedicated has more predictable baselines; tighter error budget expectations. |
| Prod | Dedicated (non-SLA / internal) | 10% | 10% -> 50% -> 100% | Blocker: +10% OR +90ms | Blocker: +12% OR +140ms | Blocker: +0.25% absolute OR 1.4x baseline (baseline floor 0.08%) | Warning: GPU util +10pp OR queue p95 +20% | N/A by default | For internal dogfood and lower-risk tenants. |
| Prod | Private (VPC) | 5% (or 1 node) | 1 node -> 25% -> 100% | Blocker: +10% OR +100ms | Blocker: +15% OR +160ms | Blocker: +0.30% absolute OR 1.5x baseline (baseline floor 0.10%) | Blocker: GPU util +12pp OR queue p95 +25% | Warning: eval score -1.0% relative (if enabled) | Private is topology-dependent; node-based canary preferred. Some customers may not have token-level telemetry. |
| Prod | Private (air-gapped / limited telemetry) | 1 node | 1 node -> 100% | Blocker: “hard failures” only (apply health + runtime errors) | Blocker: “hard failures” only | Blocker: +0.50% absolute OR 2x baseline (if available) | Warning only if available | N/A | If metrics unavailable, canary gating falls back to apply health + runtime error counters; recommend manual observation. |

TAB: Gate definitions (signals + queries)
| Gate | Type | Primary metric(s) | Query/Definition | Trip logic | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| p95 latency delta | Blocker | request_latency_ms{quantile="0.95"} | Compare canary vs baseline for same route/model/scope | Trip if above threshold for 3 consecutive 1-min buckets | Catch batching/queueing regressions and cache misses. |
| p99 latency delta | Blocker | request_latency_ms{quantile="0.99"} | Same as above | Trip if above threshold for 3 consecutive buckets | Protect tail latency (often what customers page on). |
| Error rate | Blocker | request_errors_total / requests_total | Includes 5xx, gateway timeouts, model timeouts; excludes 4xx | Trip if absolute increase OR relative multiplier exceeded | Rollback should be triggered by correctness/availability issues fast. |
| Saturation: GPU util | Blocker/Warning (tier dependent) | gpu_utilization_pct | Scope to canary pool/cluster; median across GPUs | Trip if sustained >= 10 minutes above delta threshold | Over-aggressive batching can push saturation -> queues -> latency collapse. |
| Saturation: queue depth | Blocker/Warning (tier dependent) | scheduler_queue_depth, queue_wait_ms{p95} | Compare canary vs baseline | Trip if p95 queue wait or depth exceeds delta threshold | Early detection of load shedding / head-of-line blocking. |
| OOM / runtime crash | Blocker | oom_kills_total, runtime_restarts_total | Raw counter increase in canary pool | Trip on any OOM kill OR restart rate > baseline + 1 | Quantization/profile swaps + KV cache settings can increase memory. |
| Apply health | Blocker | config_apply_success, config_apply_in_progress_age_s | Control plane apply status + runtime ack | Trip if apply stuck > 10 min OR any apply failure | Prevent “stuck canary” and partial propagation risk. |
| Quality/Evals regression (optional) | Warning/Blocker | eval_score, golden_prompt_pass_rate | If eval suite attached to route/model | Trip if below threshold for 2 consecutive eval runs (or single run for blocker tier) | Only enabled when eval plumbing exists; not required for initial release. |

TAB: Mapping to SLOs / error budgets (rough guidance)
| Tier | Typical customer promise | Budget posture | Gate tightness intention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted default | “best effort” with platform SLOs | shared error budget across many routes | Moderate: block obvious harm, avoid flapping on noisy endpoints |
| Hosted high criticality routes | internal “page on tail latency” routes | protective | Tight: prioritize reliability over cost savings |
| Dedicated SLA tenants | contract-backed SLAs (latency/uptime) | strict | Tight: less tolerance for error/lat spikes; use predictable baselines |
| Private | customer-operated + variable telemetry | mixed | Default moderate; encourage customer-defined gates; provide safe fallbacks |

TAB: Overrides & exception policy
| Override type | Allowed by | Requirements | Audit fields (must log) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temporarily loosen thresholds | SRE on-call (prod) OR tenant admin (Dedicated/Private) if permitted | Justification text + linked ticket/incident + expiration (max 24h) | actor, scope, old/new thresholds, reason, ticket, expires_at, request_id | Intended for incident mitigation when baseline is already bad / noisy. |
| Disable a gate | SRE lead approval (Sean Gallagher delegate) | Linked incident + documented fallback monitoring plan | same as above + approver | Disabling p95/p99/error gates in prod should be extremely rare. |
| Shorten canary window | Console operator with apply permission | Must still meet min sample size (>= 50k tokens OR >= 1k req) | actor, scope, window change, reason | Prevent premature promotion on tiny traffic. |
| Increase canary traffic fraction | SRE/Platform operator | Must confirm capacity headroom (GPU util < 70% baseline) | actor, scope, old/new fraction, reason | Used when wanting faster confidence during low-traffic periods. |

Notes / open questions (as of 2025-02-03)
- Baseline windows during ongoing incident: should we auto-detect and block applies? (Neha: likely yes for GA; requires incident-bot/StatusPage signal).
- For Dedicated: do we key gates on “per-tenant SLO dashboards” (Aisha) vs global route dashboards (Logan)? Need final metric label standard.
- p95/p99 absolute ms caps are coarse; may need per-model normalization for long-context routes.
- Private limited telemetry path: ensure we still gate on “apply health” + runtime error counters, and require a manual checklist step in Console.

Changelog
- 2025-02-03 (Aisha): tightened Dedicated SLA error gate from +0.20% to +0.15% absolute; clarified baseline floors.
- 2025-01-28 (Sean): added requirement for 3 consecutive datapoints to trip to reduce flakiness.
- 2025-01-16 (Aisha): initial draft from eng-sre metric gates thread + rollout PM feedback.
